bull_bear.body:
- Scale in e-commerce enablement: Cocoblu partners with 1,500+ active brand partners and sellers, up over 25% from 1,200+ a year earlier, offering approximately 8.4 million unique items
- Fulfilment reach: 520 fulfilment centres and Quick Commerce dark stores serving almost all Indian pin codes, covering 99.9% of the addressable delivery network
- Demonstrated e-commerce operating discipline: Cocoblu has been EBITDA positive since inception and served approximately 14 Crore orders in FY 2025-26, cumulatively over 45 Crore orders since March 2022
- Proprietary technology: Seller Partner (SP) API integration, AI agents automating shared-services functions, and AI tools for customer service, compliance monitoring and pricing decisions
- Distribution moat in EV: 221 Revolt dealerships across 202 cities and 24 States and Union Territories, recognised as Franchisor of the Year - Electric Vehicle at the 21st National Franchise Excellence Awards
- Differentiated EV technology stack of 3.24 kWh lithium-ion batteries, regenerative braking, smart riding modes, 4G connectivity and OTA updates, combining affordability with a low cost of ownership relative to petrol motorcycles
- Indigenous drone capability aligned to Atmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India, spanning drones, Counter-UAS, AI-enabled solutions and remote pilot training, with defence and state-police customer credentials
- Brand credibility in consumer commerce: Cocoblu holds a 5-star rating on the Amazon platform; Revolt uses cricketer Hardik Pandya as Brand Ambassador and a Formula 4 India sponsorship
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-activity and extreme customer/entity concentration at the listed-entity level — The BRSR records 100% of standalone turnover from a single activity - human resource provision and management of human resources functions (NIC 78300) - with nil plants, one national office and only 33 employees. The listed entity itself is a holding shell whose economics depend entirely on subsidiary performance.
- Narrowing EV cost advantage after GST 2.0 — Management explicitly flagged that the GST 2.0 reform effective end-September 2025 reduced ICE vehicle prices substantially, widening the price differential that had favoured EVs - a direct headwind to Revolt's affordability-led positioning.
- EV infrastructure and supply-chain dependence — The MD&A names charging infrastructure as still inadequate outside metros (fuelling range anxiety) and flags supply-chain dependence on imported critical minerals for batteries, both of which constrain volume growth and cost for the electric mobility business.
- Technology obsolescence and continuous innovation burden — Listed among the MD&A Challenges: rapid technological advancements requiring continuous innovation. The Group's e-commerce, EV and drone businesses all compete on technology stacks that must be reinvested in constantly.
- Cybersecurity threats and data privacy exposure — Listed among the MD&A Challenges as increasing cybersecurity threats and data privacy concerns - material for a group whose e-commerce platform handles ~14 Crore orders a year and which deploys AI tools for pricing and customer service.
- Regulatory risk to digital businesses — The MD&A Challenges list names regulatory developments impacting digital businesses; the Group's e-commerce, quick commerce and drone operations are all subject to evolving Indian regulation (Drone Rules, DigitalSky, marketplace rules).
- Intensifying competition across technology-driven sectors — Explicitly listed among the MD&A Challenges. Cocoblu operates as a seller on third-party marketplaces and Revolt competes in India's e-two-wheeler segment against larger OEMs, so competitive intensity directly compresses returns.
- Talent availability and high employee turnover — The MD&A flags availability of skilled talent in emerging technologies, particularly AI and semiconductor design, while the BRSR discloses a permanent-employee turnover rate of 20% in FY 2025-26 (31.4% in FY 2024-25, 40% in FY 2023-24) on a base of only 32 permanent employees.
- Geopolitical, trade and inflationary volatility — The MD&A lists geopolitical tensions and uncertainties in global trade, and inflationary pressures and fluctuations in commodity prices, among challenges; the Board's risk framework separately identifies foreign-exchange-related risks, business-competition risks and contractual risks.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: At the standalone level the Company is engaged in manpower/human resource supply and consultancy, payroll management services and related activities, serving corporates, urban and rural populations and Government customers on a pan-India basis. Its economic substance sits in wholly owned subsidiaries: Cocoblu Retail (an e-commerce enabler that sells and manages marketplace operations for 1,500+ brands and sellers), Revolt Intellicorp (electric motorcycles under the Revolt Motors brand, manufactured at Manesar, Haryana), Neobrands (a house of Gen Z fashion, lifestyle and music brands) and Neosky/Throttle Aerospace (indigenous Unmanned Aerial Systems and Counter-UAS for defence, government, enterprise and commercial customers). The Group positions itself at the convergence of digital commerce, electric mobility and autonomous systems.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **E-commerce (Cocoblu Retail):** Marketplace seller and brand-enablement services on Amazon and other marketplaces, Quick commerce via Amazon Now, Brand partnerships including Flying Machine, Gap, Fila, Lotto, Chumbak
- **Consumer brands (Neobrands):** Fyltr (Western Clothing), INKD (Denim), Pump'd (Athleisure), Kaari (Ethnic Premium), Kalaanj (Ethnic Economy), Akkord (Musical Instruments), Neomate (Stationery)
- **Electric vehicles (Revolt Motors):** Electric motorcycles with 3.24 kWh lithium-ion batteries, regenerative braking, smart riding modes and 4G-connected mobile controls with OTA updates
- **Drones (Neosky / Throttle Aerospace):** Indigenous Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS), Specialised surveillance drones, Counter-UAS and AI-enabled aerial intelligence solutions, Drone pilot training, system integration and consultancy
- **Standalone (RattanIndia Enterprises):** Manpower / human resource supply and consultancy, Payroll management services

outlook.body:
- Invest in businesses that combine cutting-edge technologies with scalable business models in sectors benefiting from strong structural demand - identifying high-potential opportunities early and building scalable platforms through disciplined capital allocation
- Build a diversified technology-led portfolio positioned at the convergence of artificial intelligence, digital commerce, electric mobility, autonomous systems and advanced manufacturing
- Cocoblu: scale the e-commerce enablement platform further while deepening brand partnerships, supported by a robust vendor ecosystem and technology-driven operations
- Cocoblu: expand the premium brand portfolio (Flying Machine, Gap, Fila, Lotto, Chumbak and D2C brands) to improve revenue quality, and scale the newly entered quick-commerce channel via Amazon Now
- Cocoblu: build in-house technology - Seller Partner (SP) API integration, AI agents for shared services, and AI tools for customer service, compliance monitoring and pricing decisions
- Revolt: manufacturing scale-up at the Manesar, Haryana facility to meet rising domestic and international demand while ensuring supply chain efficiency
- Revolt: geographic expansion of the dealership network across India with a focus on Tier-I and Tier-II cities, and entry into new international markets beyond Nepal and Sri Lanka
- Revolt: product line diversification across consumer segments from urban commuters to performance seekers, plus continued brand building, digital engagement and strategic partnerships
- Revolt: continue leveraging PM E-DRIVE Scheme subsidies to reduce consumer costs and accelerate EV adoption
- Neobrands: scale international presence (UAE, KSA, United States, Canada, Mexico, and the Noon marketplace in the GCC) and expand the portfolio beyond core soft-lines and apparel into new lifestyle categories
- Neobrands: deliberate investment in brand building and advertising to establish long-term consumer recall for its Gen Z brand portfolio
- Drones: develop indigenous technologies aligned with Atmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India, and build multiple revenue streams through system integration, value-added services, pilot training, consultancy and lifecycle support
- Group: internal restructuring - the entire shareholding in Cocoblu Retail was transferred to Neobrands after year-end, making Cocoblu a direct wholly owned subsidiary of Neobrands and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of the Company
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion in FY 2025-26 was footprint- and network-led rather than plant-led. Revolt Intellicorp expanded its dealership network to 221 dealerships covering 202 cities across 24 States and Union Territories, rolled out its 50,000th electric motorcycle from the Manesar, Haryana facility, and achieved ISO 9001:2015 certification; going forward Revolt plans to ramp up production capacity at Manesar in the upcoming years, expand dealerships with a focus on Tier-I and Tier-II cities, and enter new international markets beyond Nepal and Sri Lanka, where it participated in the Colombo Motor Show 2025. Cocoblu Retail expanded fulfilment infrastructure to 520 fulfilment centres and Quick Commerce dark stores, grew active vendors by over 25% from 1,200+ to 1,500+, widened its catalogue to approximately 8.4 million unique items covering 99.9% of India's addressable delivery network, entered quick commerce through Amazon Now, and built in-house technology via a Seller Partner (SP) API integration and AI agents for shared services. Neobrands expanded internationally into UAE, Saudi Arabia, the United States, Canada and Mexico and started operations on the Noon marketplace in the GCC, extended its portfolio beyond core soft-lines, and received a Rs. 350 Crore capital infusion as part of a group restructuring under which it became the intermediate holding company for Cocoblu Retail, completed in April 2026. The Drone Business continued to invest in engineering, product development, manufacturing infrastructure, quality systems and skilled manpower to build a scalable operating platform. At the standalone listed-entity level the BRSR records nil plants and a single national office. During the year Neorise Global Trading L.L.C S.O.C was incorporated in mainland Dubai on 24 November 2025 as a wholly owned subsidiary of Neorise Technologies - FZCO.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India is expected to remain one of the fastest-growing major economies globally during FY 2026-27, with rising urbanisation, favourable demographics, sustained infrastructure investment, manufacturing expansion and rapid digitalisation supporting long-term growth
- Technology-led businesses are expected to remain among the fastest-growing segments of the economy, with AI, fintech, electric mobility, e-commerce, cloud infrastructure, digital healthcare and consumer internet platforms driving the next phase of value creation
- The global economy is expected to remain resilient during FY 2026-27, supported by moderating inflation, gradual monetary easing and increasing investment in digital technologies
- India's digital economy is being propelled by over one billion internet connections, UPI as the world's largest real-time digital payments ecosystem, and initiatives such as Digital India, the IndiaAI Mission, ONDC, India Stack, DigiLocker and 5G rollout
- EV demand: India's EV industry crossed 2.5 million units in FY2025-26, a 25% year-on-year increase, with the market shifting from subsidy-driven to one built on scale, industry readiness and regulatory maturity, in line with NITI Aayog's blueprint for a 30% EV share by 2030
- EV opportunity set: rising Tier-2/Tier-3 city adoption, battery technology localisation, PLI-backed manufacturing, and electrification of commercial fleets (e-rickshaws, e-cargo, e-buses) as the fastest-scaling segment
- Drone demand: geopolitical conflicts (Russia-Ukraine, Middle East) and Operation Sindoor have reinforced the strategic importance of drones, loitering munitions and counter-drone technologies; restrictions on drone imports and increasing preference for Indian manufacturers in defence procurement create a favourable environment, supported by the Government's vision of making India a global drone manufacturing hub by 2030
- Policy tailwinds for EV: the PM E-DRIVE Scheme succeeding FAME II, PLI schemes for Advanced Chemistry Cell batteries and auto components, charging infrastructure expansion and reduced import duties for global players manufacturing locally
- Margin/efficiency lever: improving operating leverage, stronger business fundamentals and an unwavering focus on efficiency contributed significantly to performance during the year
- Cocoblu's technology-led operating model, expanding fulfilment network and entry into quick commerce provide a foundation for continued scale and sustainable profitability
- Headwind: the September 2025 GST 2.0 reform reduced ICE vehicle prices substantially, narrowing the cost advantage EVs had relied on, alongside inadequate charging infrastructure outside metros and supply-chain dependence on imported critical minerals for batteries
